title: RAW: lexical-site spelling memory reuses a recent ligature choice across unrelated intervening words
summary: Complete invented stochastic writer: one fixed AB-to-C fusion preserves all source content, but each exact source word and eligible site keeps its own last written choice. At its next occurrence the choice stays with probability3/4 and flips with1/4. Reader expands C to AB. Distinct prediction is recurrence-ordered spelling persistence after accounting for static word/site and local-flank effects, not another word-frequency gain or native carrier-cover test.

design.mechanism: A learned lexical spelling trace persists between repetitions of the same word; writing unrelated words does not overwrite that trace. This represents a specific scribal-memory hypothesis, not an attested medieval practice or a claim that any Voynich shapes are ligatures.
design.source_and_inventory: Source is any finite list of nonempty words over21 abstract units. Choose distinct source units A and B; add one reserved output token C, not a source unit. A fixed bijection maps these22 abstract output tokens to22 working units. No unit receives a sound or meaning. Word spaces and explicit document start/end are preserved; no hidden paragraph/line resets. This restricted source inventory is paid and is not asserted to describe a natural language.
writer: Initially every lexical-site memory bit is0, allocating a bit on first use. Key is the COMPLETE source word and the starting index of an AB occurrence in that source word. SinceA!=B, AB opportunities do not overlap.

For each opportunity, independently flip its stored bit with probability1/4 before emission, otherwise keep it. Emit C if the new bit is1, or emit A followed by B if0. Preserve every source unit outside opportunities exactly, and retain source word order and spaces.

Store the new bit under the same exact word/site key. Multiple eligible sites in one word have separate bits; no forced all-fused/all-unfused word choice. Unrelated words neither update nor erase this key.
design.reader: Invert the fixed output bijection; replace every C byAB, leave the other21tokens literal, retain word boundaries. This uniquely returns the source words without knowing random choices or the memory state. The writing choices are not source-message information and are not claimed recoverable as an original random seed. Every observed choice has a defined likelihood under the memory process.
design.state_cost: One bit per previously encountered eligible exact word/site, plus the stored word strings/site addresses needed to find those bits. Memory is unbounded with vocabulary, explicitly charged; no claim of a tiny finite-state writer. The table is spelling memory, not a freely learned semantic dictionary.
design.joint_positive_motivation: Directed source order and the fixed asymmetric AB fusion retain productive parts. Repeated complete word identities select separate memory histories, potentially contributing whole-word effects. Spelling varies by the preceding occurrence of that SAME word/site, rather than only by current neighbors. These are proposed explanations, not measured fits to the existing positive findings.
design.prediction: Afterm subsequent visits to one lexical-site memory, the chance its bit matches the earlier bit is(1+2**(-m))/2. The number or identity of intervening unrelated words does not enter this law. With fixed endpoint states and fixed fused/unfused occurrence totals, a within-key path probability is proportional to(1/3)**switch_count; clustered histories are favored over freely exchangeable orderings.
design.contrast: Static per-word spelling preferences can yield repeated preferred forms without temporal memory. Global pen-style drift can correlate different words by physical proximity. This model instead predicts additional dependence specifically on recurrence order of the same word/site, surviving those rivals if the physical/opportunity binding is correct.
design.example: For source ABX repeated three times, one allowed choice history0,1,1 yields ABX / CX / CX; intervening Ywords leave its memory unchanged. This is a source-free illustration, not a native reading.
design.smallest_future_test: Only after an independently justified expansion/opportunity contract, freeze repeated exact-word/site episodes and compare their transition counts with a static model while controlling page/hand and actual local flanks. Preserve endpoints when conditioning within episodes so outside transitions do not change. Require genuinely mobile histories and compare lexical-recurrence distance against intervening other-word distance. No new native census or statistical procedure is selected by this card. A transition rate near1/2, absence of excess same-key persistence, or persistence explained solely by physical-neighbor drift would contradict this fixed3/4retention model at adequate capacity.
limits: A latent source word/site is not identified merely because two analyst-expanded strings match. An actual fusion binding remains a condition.
Full native coverage under theC-expansion is automatic and is NOT an achievement; the temporal law is the falsifiable content.
The1/4flip law is an explicit modeling choice, not an estimated historical constant; do not retune it after a failed test.
No finite corpus, source language, semantics, key recovery or full statistical fit is claimed.
